notes: The statutory rates now live in your ledger instead of inside the app. The PAYE bands, personal reliefs, SSNIT and pension rates, the concessionary bonus and overtime rules and the withholding de-minimis threshold were built into each version — so a Ghana budget change needed a new release from us and a reinstall from you, and if that did not happen before the first payroll run of the new year the run was wrong permanently: a payslip is a frozen record, so the wrong figures stay in it and are carried into the PAYE return. There is now an Administration ▸ Statutory Rates screen showing the bands, rates and reliefs the app would compute with on any date you choose and where they came from, and an administrator can enter a new set the day the budget is published, dated from when it takes effect. THE DATE DECIDES: the app uses the set in force on the date of the entry it is computing, so a payroll for March uses March's rates even if you run it in May, and a set entered now for next January cannot reach back over this year. Nothing already computed changes — payslips keep the figures they were run with. A set is saved complete, prefilled from what is in force, so you change only the figures that moved and it never depends on an earlier set. Until somebody enters a set the app uses exactly the rates it always has: this release changes no figure anywhere. Payroll also names the set it used for each month, and if it cannot read the rates it says so and asks you not to run payroll rather than quietly falling back. Also: clearer VAT-return wording — an input-VAT account is only needed if you reclaim VAT on purchases; if you do not, there is nothing to set off and you remit the output figure in full, which is what the app has always done and now says. No posting rule and no report changed.
